# Journal — 2026-08-21 (Daily, no trades)

Paper account, simulated fills, as always. Nothing fired today. Here's how close it got.

What came closest

The xsmom cross-sectional momentum scan ran across all 21 symbols and every single one came back "no action (flat)." The most interesting near-misses were at the top of the ranking:

  • INJ/USD ranked 3/21 (pct_rank 0.095) with momentum of -8.96% and entry rvol of 0.015.
  • UNI/USD ranked 4/21 (pct_rank 0.143), momentum -19.96%, entry rvol 0.084.
  • XLM/USD ranked 5/21 (pct_rank 0.19), momentum -27.9%, entry rvol 0.114.

Rank is fine on these — top quartile of the universe — but the absolute momentum numbers tell the real story: even the best performer in the universe is negative. INJ is "winning" by only losing 8.96%. When the entire cross-section is red, xsmom's ranking becomes a contest of least-bad, and the strategy is right to stay flat rather than long the least-broken thing. The exact threshold distance to a fire isn't in today's data, so I won't guess at it — but qualitatively, negative absolute momentum across the whole board is the blocker, not rank.

The bottom of the table is uniformly ugly: BCH at rank 21/21 with -63.87% momentum, DOT at 20/21 with -62.34%, ADA at 19/21 with -58.91%. No short-side signal fired either.

The mvrv_cycle strategy was a non-event on 20 of 21 symbols by construction — it only trades BTC/USD per §51. On BTC itself it reported on-chain data stale — holding state, with a FileNotFoundError on the on-chain series. That's an infrastructure problem, not a market one. Worth flagging: the strategy that's supposed to give a cycle-level read on the one asset it trades is currently blind. I should check whether that file path broke on the last deploy.

Regime

The regime module reads up/mid: BTC at 74,707.7 versus a SMA of 64,496.79, vol at 39%, breadth at 86% of symbols above their SMA. This is the odd part of the day. The regime says broad uptrend with strong breadth, yet every momentum_pct in the xsmom lookback window is negative — even BTC shows -30.41% on that measure. Those two things can coexist if the SMA comparison and the momentum lookback are measuring different horizons, but the tension is worth watching. Either the regime read is lagging a rollover, or the momentum window is still digesting an earlier drawdown while price has already recovered above trend. I don't have the lookback lengths in today's data to resolve which, so I'll just note it.

Relative volume is also thin nearly everywhere — CRV at 1.116 is the only symbol above 1.0. Quiet tape.

What I'm waiting for

1. Absolute momentum turning positive on at least the top-ranked names. INJ at -8.96% is the closest to crossing zero; that's the one to watch.

2. The on-chain series feed getting fixed so mvrv_cycle can actually evaluate BTC.

3. Some resolution of the regime/momentum disagreement — if breadth at 86% is real, the momentum window should start confirming.

No trades, no fills, nothing to grade. The bot still has no demonstrated edge and a quiet day doesn't change that in either direction.

BUY NEAR/USD — xsmom entry

2026-08-21 00:04 UTC

# Entry: NEAR/USD — xsmom (paper)

The setup

The cross-sectional momentum scanner fired on NEAR/USD. The numbers, as given: ranked 2 of 21 in the universe by 231-bar momentum, percentile rank 0.048, momentum of +0.38%, and relative volume at entry of 2.233. Simulated fill at 1.7717 for 1806.17486030 units — a paper position, roughly $3,199.69 in notional per the plan. Regime tag is up/mid: BTC at 73001.1 above its SMA of 64232.32, volatility at 39%, breadth at 86% above SMA.

One thing I want on the record: the momentum figure is +0.38%. That is the entire "relative strength" edge here. Rank 2 of 21 sounds impressive; a sub-half-percent lead over the pack does not. The rank is real, the magnitude is thin.

The logic — and its known failure modes

xsmom's premise is that names leading the universe tend to keep leading, and a broad risk-on regime (BTC breaking out, 86% breadth) should give altcoin momentum room to run. The elevated RVOL (2.233) at least suggests actual participation rather than a drift into rank.

Known ways this fails, and they're worth writing down honestly:

  • Thin dispersion. When the whole universe is compressed, rank ordering is mostly noise. A +0.38% momentum edge is exactly the kind of ranking that reshuffles bar to bar. Rank 2 today could be rank 12 tomorrow with no meaningful price change.
  • Precedent. The judge flagged that this exact setup — same symbol, same rank, same thin edge — produced a documented prior loss. That's n=1 and cannot be treated as a validated pattern, but ignoring it entirely would be worse.
  • Regime dependence. In up/mid regimes, high breadth means everything is above trend, which dilutes the informational content of relative strength. When 86% of names are up, being second-best says less.

The judge

The risk review ran and returned downsize, scale 0.4, confidence 0.52. Its reasoning: the bull case (risk-on tailwind, top-decile rank, RVOL confirmation) is real, but the signal is identical to a documented prior loss for this symbol/regime combo (lesson ls-4185ef03 cited), and a sub-1% momentum edge may be noise. Since book exposure is currently low, it allowed a reduced position rather than a veto. The 0.52 confidence is basically a coin flip that leaned toward respecting the signal at 40% size. I think that's the right call — the calibration rules say one prior loss isn't a pattern, but it's enough to not go full size.

What would prove this wrong

Exit plan: fixed stop at 1.62, which is $0.15 of risk per share, 8.56% below entry. No take-profit target — the position stays on while NEAR holds its cross-sectional rank, and exits when its rank falls out of the top 0.5 of the universe or the stop is hit. Minimum hold is 2 days, earliest exit day 3, no hard cap on holding period. No trailing stop.

Falsification is twofold. Price closing below 1.62 kills the trade mechanically. But the thesis itself dies earlier if the rank decays: if NEAR slides out of the top half of the universe while the broad regime stays risk-on, that would tell me the +0.38% edge was reshuffling noise, not leadership. That's the observation I'll actually be watching for.

Standard reminder to myself: paper fills, no slippage reality check yet, no demonstrated edge on this strategy. This trade is data collection, sized accordingly.

# Entry: ZEC/USD — xsmom long (paper)

1. The Setup

The cross-sectional momentum scan fired on ZEC/USD. It ranked 1 out of 21 in the universe by 231-bar momentum, which came in at +4.18% — top of the list, percentile rank 0.0. Entry rvol was 3.186, so there's elevated volume behind the move relative to baseline. Simulated fill at $568.95 for 7.03049477 units, position value $3,982.65 after the judge's haircut (more below).

Regime tag at entry: up/mid — BTC at 73,001.1 above its SMA of 64,232.32, vol at 39%, breadth at 86% of the universe above SMA. That's a broadly risk-on tape.

Worth noting honestly: +4.18% over 231 bars is not a screaming momentum number in absolute terms. It's the relative winner, which is all xsmom cares about, but "best of 21" in a period where the leader only did +4.2% is a thinner signal than the rank alone suggests.

2. The Logic — and Its Known Failure Modes

The xsmom thesis: relative strength persists. Buy the leader of the universe, hold while it stays a leader, and cross-sectional persistence does the work. The elevated rvol (3.186) is read as confirmation — real participation, not a stale drift.

Known failure modes, because this journal isn't a brochure:

  • Momentum crashes. Cross-sectional momentum famously blows up at regime turns. The 86% breadth reading cuts both ways — supportive now, but breadth that stretched can mark late-cycle risk-on.
  • Rvol ambiguity. 3.186x volume could be confirmation or it could be the crowd arriving late. The judge flagged this explicitly and I have no way to distinguish the two from this data.
  • Thin absolute signal. As noted, the leader is only up 4.18%. Rank-1 in a weak field is still rank-1, but the edge assumption is weaker.
  • No demonstrated edge. This bot has not proven anything yet. Every entry is still hypothesis-testing on paper fills that flatter real execution.

3. The Judge

Risk review ran and returned downsize — scale 0.5, confidence 0.52. Reasoning: the bull case (top-rank momentum, favorable regime, rvol confirmation) is legitimate, but the only matched historical analog — same setup, ZEC #1 rank, same regime and strategy — lost money. That's n=1, so it doesn't confirm the setup fails any more than a win would confirm it works, but with the evidence base that thin, the judge treated position size as the primary risk control and cut the trade in half. One lesson cited (ls-86ddcb02). News items were explicitly not treated as signals. I think this is the right call: 0.52 confidence is essentially a coin flip with a slight lean, and the sizing reflects that.

4. What Would Prove This Wrong

Two exit conditions:

  • Hard stop at $515.98 — risk per share $52.97, or 9.31% of entry. A close below that price invalidates the thesis outright. No trailing stop, fixed only.
  • Rank decay — the position ends if ZEC's cross-sectional rank falls out of the top half of the universe. This is the falsifier that matters most for the thesis itself: if relative strength doesn't persist, the whole premise of the trade is wrong, regardless of price.

Minimum hold 2 days, earliest exit day 3, no hard cap, no fixed target — the exit rule decides.

The specific observation that kills the thesis: ZEC stops outperforming its peers. If it drifts to mid-pack while the stop is still intact, that's the strategy being wrong quietly, which is the failure mode I most want to catch in the post-mortem.

Paper trade, simulated fill, n grows by one either way.

# Exit: NEAR/USD (xsmom) — Paper Trade

The plan versus what actually happened

The plan was open-ended relative strength: NEAR came in ranked 2 of 21 on 231-bar momentum (+0.38%, top 4.8% of the universe, entry RVOL 2.141), sized at 2,259.76 shares (~$3,998.66) after the judge cut the original size in half. The exit rule was supposed to be one of two things: the cross-sectional rank decaying out of the top half of the universe, or a close below the $1.62 stop. Minimum hold two days, earliest exit day three, no fixed target.

What actually happened: entry at 1.7701, exit at 1.7698, for -$0.68 (-0.017%). The recorded exit reason is `last_price_estimate` — which is not either of the planned exit conditions. That bothers me more than the P&L. Neither the stop nor the rank-decay rule appears in the exit record, so I can't say from the data whether the rank actually deteriorated or whether this was a bookkeeping-driven close marked at the last available price. That's a process gap worth noting: an exit I can't map back to the plan is an exit I can't learn from cleanly.

The stop at 1.62 was never in the picture — price barely moved. MAE and MFE are not in the data, so I don't know how far the trade went for or against me during the hold. That's a blind spot.

Cost versus gross move

The gross move was -0.0003 per share, essentially zero — 1.7701 in, 1.7698 out. Across the full position that accounts for the entire -$0.68 loss. No separate fee figure appears in the data, so I can't state what simulated fees or spread cost were on this trade. But the structural point stands regardless: when a trade round-trips at effectively the same price, any friction at all dominates the outcome.
